name: GLM-4.5
attention_variant: GQA (standard) - NOT MLA despite the DeepSeek-derived MoE design
notes: CONTRADICTS A COMMON ASSUMPTION: GLM-4.5 does NOT use MLA. Its config has no kv_lora_rank; it has num_key_value_heads 8 and the HF reference implementation Glm4MoeAttention is plain GQA (kv_a_proj_with_mqa is absent). MLA arrived back in the GLM line only at GLM-4.7. Worth stating plainly because GLM is usually assumed to be DeepSeek-derived. Consequence for serving, and this is the worst KV economics of any 32B-active model in this slice: kv_cache_bytes_per_token = 92 layers x 8 kv_heads x head_dim 128 x 2 (K and V) x 2 bytes (bf16) = 92 x 8 x 128 x 2 x 2 = 376,832 B/token (368 KiB). DeepSeek-V3 does 37B active in 68.6 KiB/token. GLM-4.5 does 32B active in 368 KiB/token - 5.4x the KV for slightly less compute. At 128k context that is 46 GiB of KV per sequence versus 8.58 GiB. On long-context batch serving this is the deciding constraint, not FLOPs. Vendor: 355B total / 32B active (safetensors total 358.34B). Our config arithmetic gives 352.7B / 33.6B, matching to ~1%. MoE: 160 routed + 1 shared, 8 per token, first_k_dense_replace 3, n_group 1 / topk_group 1 (no grouped routing, unlike DeepSeek's 8 groups). routed_scaling_factor 2.5. hidden 5120, 92 layers, 96 heads / 8 kv heads (gqa_ratio 12), head_dim 128, intermediate 12288, moe_intermediate_size 1536. partial_rotary_factor 0.5. Context 131072 native, rope_theta 1000000, rope_scaling null. MIT. num_nextn_predict_layers 1.
